# Mixed bridge contract ownership

This owned hierarchy combines original checked parameter bridges with method-owned covariant result bridges on the same Signature-free child. A typed read invokes the generic fluent member, so both original bridge families participate in each completed call.

Five frozen call routes cover typed, raw and generic interface calls plus special entry into both original parameter bridges. Future subclass overrides cover both families. Each of 240 fresh JVM cases runs twice, checking receiver, key, method input, opaque result and final result identities, callbacks, partial writes, original checked casts, null timing, and exact runtime, Error and checked failures. The opaque generic result can be null, an unrelated parent, or a replacement chosen during a callback.

Every recovered Java unit must compile with every original definition, access/Code role, bridge, method Signature and Exceptions. Canonical covariance proofs are reused only for their exact original ancestor contracts; compiler bridge projections keep their original unverified detail status. Independent wrong programs and Code-preserving Signature controls qualify the observers.
